::: {#def-attention}

#### Scaled dot-product attention

**Scaled dot-product attention** takes $m$ queries,
the rows of an $m \times d_k$ matrix $\matr{Q}$,
and $n$ keys and $n$ values,
the rows of an $n \times d_k$ matrix $\matr{K}$ and an $n \times d_v$ matrix $\matr{V}$.
It returns the $m \times d_v$ matrix

$$
\operatorname{Attention}\paren{\matr{Q}, \matr{K}, \matr{V}}
\eqdef
\operatorname{softmax}\paren{\frac{\matr{Q} \tp{\matr{K}}}{\sqrt{d_k}}} \matr{V},
$$

with the [softmax](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/multiclass-logistic-regression.html#def-softmax) taken across each row
[@vaswani2017attention, section 3.2.1].
Row $i$ of the softmax holds weights $\attnweight_{i1}, \dots, \attnweight_{in}$,
which are positive and sum to 1,
so row $i$ of the output is a weighted average of the rows of $\matr{V}$.
@bahdanau2015neural scored each key with a small network instead of a [dot product](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-vectors.html#def-dot-product),
and some sources call that form additive attention.

:::
